metadata.aggregate_power_guardrail: The visible 1,036 MW Total Baseload Power is the aggregate of the 536 MW planned grid total and 500 MW planned behind-the-meter generation. It creates no third capacity row and must never be summed with those components as additional capacity.

metadata.capacity_overlap_guardrail: The 116 MW contracted grid row is contained in the 536 MW planned total grid row, while 500 MW is a different planned generation metric. These observations are scenario and stage facts, not additive current load or energy consumption.

evidence.title: AVAIO Digital Breaks Ground on $6 Billion Brandon Data Center Campus; Leading Mississippi Contractor Begins Site Work
evidence.excerpt: AVAIO's September 2025 release says Taurus site work was officially underway and describes the first phase as more than 600,000 square feet of data-center buildings with 116 MW of power capacity.

capacities.notes: Executed Entergy Mississippi electric-service agreement for the initial 116 MW of grid power. The source forecasts energization in June 2027, but no exact target day is invented. This contracted grid observation is contained in the separately reported planned 536 MW grid total and is not installed, energized, operational, current load, critical IT load, gross facility demand, consumption, or annual energy.

Visible official page total for planned campus grid power: the initial 116 MW plus an additional 420 MW guided for availability by end 2030. This total contains the contracted 116 MW row; neither the 420 MW increment nor the 116 MW component may be added to 536 MW as separate total grid capacity. It is not installed, energized, operational, current draw, critical IT load, gross facility demand, consumption, or annual energy.

Planned onsite behind-the-meter thermal-generation capacity/nameplate reported by AVAIO. This future 500 MW is the generation component of the visible 1,036 MW aggregate baseload claim; 1,036 MW creates no additional row. The 500 MW is not installed or operating generation, current output, data-center load, grid supply, consumption, annual energy, or PUE.
